newsitem.title: USA: IMF approves $391 million loan for Egypt.
newsitem.headline: IMF approves $391 million loan for Egypt.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund said on Friday it had approved a $391 million loan for Egypt in a show of support for its efforts to speed up economic growth and transform its economy.
Cairo does not intend to draw down on the two-year stand-by loan because its foreign currency reserves are ample, the IMF said in a statement.
The Fund's move should pave the way for a decision by the Paris Club of creditor countries to write off $4 billion of Egyptian debt.

"The (Egyptian) government sees the principal challenge for the medium term to be that of increasing economic growth so as to create employment oppurtunities for a rapidly growing population," the IMF said.

The government aims to lift economic growth to about five percent in 1997/1998 from 4.5 percent in 1996/97 and 4.2 percent in 1995/96, while cutting inflation to six percent. Consumer prices rose an estimated 7.1 pct in 1995/96.
To achieve that, Cairo intends to broaden and intensify its structural economic reforms through privatisation, deregulation, trade liberalisation and fiscal and financial reform.

"A central goal of the programme is to bring about a fundamental change in the ownership structure of the Egyptian economy," the IMF said, noting that state-owned firms account for as much as one-third of Egypt's manufacturing sector.

Besides increased privatisation, other planned reforms include transformation of the general sales tax into a value added tax; a simplification and broadening of the income tax system; and a further strengthening of banking supervision.
"Egypt needs to continue its structural reforms if it is to...exploit its considerable potential," the IMF said.
